accounts.summary: MongoDB-compatible, not MongoDB: FerretDB over PostgreSQL, covering CRUD, indexes and the wire protocol. Multi-document transactions are not supported. Runs on a CloudNativePG cluster, so failover, backup and point-in-time recovery are the operator's.

create.name: create
create.summary: Create or replace a Document database account.

flags.name: --backup-enabled
flags.summary: Whether continuous backup and WAL archiving run. ⚠ Off by default, and only because there is no destination to default to: turning it on without a destinationPath below renders no backup configuration at all rather than an empty one, so the two properties have to be set together.

flags.name: --class
flags.summary: StorageClass name for the PostgreSQL volumes. Empty means the cluster default.

flags.name: --cluster-id
flags.summary: The cluster whose namespace holds the PostgreSQL cluster and the FerretDB gateway.

flags.name: --cpu
flags.summary: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --destination-path
flags.summary: Object-store URL for base backups and WAL, for example s3://tenant-bucket/documentdb. Empty means no backup configuration is rendered, whatever enabled says.

flags.name: --instances
flags.summary: Number of PostgreSQL instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only. Failover, replication and point-in-time recovery are CloudNativePG's, which is why this row costs 1.2 engineer-months rather than a rebuild of them.

flags.name: --location
flags.summary: The region the account is billed in.

flags.name: --memory
flags.summary: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --monitoring-enabled
flags.summary: Whether both halves of this service are scraped: CloudNativePG is asked for a PodMonitor over the PostgreSQL pods, and the platform writes one over the FerretDB pods because FerretDB has no operator to ask. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production".

flags.name: --name
flags.summary: The resource's name within its group.

flags.name: --preset
flags.summary: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Databases use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

flags.name: --replicas
flags.summary: Number of FerretDB pods. The gateway is stateless — it translates and forwards, and every byte is in PostgreSQL — so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

flags.name: --resource-group
flags.summary: The resource group. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

flags.name: --retention-days
flags.summary: How long base backups and WAL are kept. The point-in-time-recovery window is this number of days.

flags.name: --size
flags.summary: Data volume size per PostgreSQL instance, in Kubernetes quantity form. Every instance carries a full copy, so raw consumption is this times the instance count. Grows online; never shrinks.

flags.name: --subscription
flags.summary: The subscription. Defaults to the current profile.

flags.name: --tags
flags.summary: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

flags.name: --tenant
flags.summary: The tenant. Defaults to the current profile.

flags.name: --version
flags.summary: FerretDB minor version. ⚠ One property moves two images: the DocumentDB PostgreSQL extension and the FerretDB gateway are released as a matched pair and a mismatched pair is a proxy talking to an extension it does not know. FerretDB maintains no long-term branch, so the two values here are the two most recent releases and a third is a new api-version.

kafka-clusters.name: kafka-clusters
kafka-clusters.title: Kafka cluster
kafka-clusters.summary: A managed Apache Kafka cluster on Strimzi in KRaft mode, with Cruise Control, configurable retention and an optional firewalled external listener.

create.name: create
create.summary: Create or replace a Kafka cluster.

flags.name: --allowed-cidrs
flags.summary: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

flags.name: --class
flags.summary: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

flags.name: --cluster-id
flags.summary: The cluster whose namespace holds the Strimzi objects.

flags.name: --cpu
flags.summary: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --cruise-control-enabled
flags.summary: Whether Cruise Control runs. On by default: docs/plan/12 puts it in the chart rather than in a follow-up, because rebalancing a Kafka cluster by hand is the operational cost that makes this the most demanding service in the catalogue.

flags.name: --delete-claim
flags.summary: Whether deleting the resource also deletes the log volumes. Off by default, so a mistaken delete leaves the data recoverable by hand.

flags.name: --external-enabled
flags.summary: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

flags.name: --hours
flags.summary: Default retention in hours. A week by default.

flags.name: --location
flags.summary: The region the cluster is billed in.

flags.name: --memory
flags.summary: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --min-in-sync-replicas
flags.summary: How many replicas must acknowledge a write before it is committed. Must be below the replication factor, or the cluster cannot tolerate one broker restart.

flags.name: --monitoring-enabled
flags.summary: Whether the operator runs a Kafka Exporter alongside the cluster, exposing consumer-lag and topic metrics to the platform's metrics stack.

flags.name: --name
flags.summary: The resource's name within its group.

flags.name: --nodes
flags.summary: Number of Kafka nodes, each acting as both a KRaft controller and a broker. Use an odd number: a quorum of two tolerates no failures, and one is a single point of failure offered for development only.

flags.name: --partitions
flags.summary: Default partition count for a new topic.

flags.name: --preset
flags.summary: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

flags.name: --replication-factor
flags.summary: Default replication factor for a new topic. Must not exceed the node count, or every produce to a new topic fails.

flags.name: --resource-group
flags.summary: The resource group. docs/plan/06 § The hierarchy.

flags.name: --retention-size
flags.summary: Default retention by partition size, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means retention is by time alone.

flags.name: --storage-size
flags.summary: Log volume size per node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

flags.name: --subscription
flags.summary: The subscription. Defaults to the current profile.

flags.name: --tags
flags.summary: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

flags.name: --tenant
flags.summary: The tenant. Defaults to the current profile.

create.name: create
create.summary: Create or replace a RabbitMQ cluster.

flags.name: --additional

flags.name: --class
flags.summary: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.

flags.name: --cluster-id
flags.summary: The cluster whose namespace holds the RabbitmqCluster.

flags.name: --cpu
flags.summary: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

flags.name: --default-type
flags.summary: The queue type a client gets when it declares a queue without asking for one. Quorum by default — docs/plan/12: a quorum queue is replicated through Raft across the nodes above, and on 4.x a classic queue is not replicated at all, so leaving this unset would put a single-node queue on a cluster the tenant paid three nodes for. This is a node-wide fallback: a vhost created with its own default queue type overrides it.

flags.name: --location
flags.summary: The region the cluster is billed in.

flags.name: --max-message-size
flags.summary: Largest message a client may publish, in bytes. Raising it costs memory on every node that holds a copy, which for a quorum queue is all of them.

flags.name: --idle-timeout-minutes
flags.summary: How long a shell may sit with nobody typing into it before it is reclaimed. The home volume survives; the pod does not. ⚠ There is no value meaning never — an idle terminal is a tenant paying for something they closed.

flags.name: --location
flags.summary: The region the console is billed in.

flags.name: --max-duration-hours
flags.summary: The longest a single shell may run, busy or not. Enforced by the kubelet through the pod's own deadline, so it holds even when nothing of this platform is running.

flags.name: --preset
flags.summary: How much a shell gets. The ladder stops at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, which is docs/plan/19's ceiling for this row — a workload that needs more needs a cluster and a job rather than a terminal.

flags.name: --principal-id
flags.summary: The managed identity every command in this shell acts as. It may not be changed: a console whose identity moved would have an audit trail describing a shell that no longer exists.

flags.name: --resource-group

flags.name: --retention-days
flags.summary: How long $HOME is kept after the console was last attached to. ⚠ Nothing sweeps on it yet — it is carried so that a console created today is swept correctly by whatever does.

flags.name: --session-recording
flags.summary: Whether everything typed into and printed by this shell is recorded. ⚠ Off by default and immutable afterwards: a shell contains secrets, a keystroke log is a liability, and a recording that could be switched off mid-life would be worth nothing to the compliance requirement it exists for.

flags.name: --size
flags.summary: The size of $HOME. It grows and never shrinks: a PersistentVolumeClaim refuses a decrease at the API.
